rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan deters worship by persuading people that the afterlife is unreal or worship useless, then emphasizing its fatigue and hardship.
rows.anchor: يقرر أولا عنده أنه لا فائدة فيه وتقريره من وجهين

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Some exegetes say Satan promises that neither Paradise nor Hell exists.
rows.anchor: أي بأنه لا جنة ولا نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other exegetes understand Satan's promise as postponing repentance.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : { وعدهم } بتسويف التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other exegetes understand the promise as false hopes, like Satan's assurance to Adam that the forbidden tree would make them angels or immortal.
rows.anchor: بالأماني الباطلة مثل قوله لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other exegetes include promises of idols' intercession, noble ancestry, and preference for immediate pleasures over the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وعدهم بشفاعة الأصنام عند الله تعالى وبالأنساب الشريفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these promises fit his account of Satan's deceptions; he directs readers seeking a fuller inventory to al-Ghazali's Book of Censure of Delusion.
rows.anchor: فهذه الأقسام كثيرة وكلها داخلة في الضبط الذي ذكرناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan calls only to appetite, anger, or status and rank, never to knowing or serving God.
rows.anchor: إنما يدعو إلى أحد أمور ثلاثة قضاء الشهوة وإمضاء الغضب وطلب الرياسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These worldly pleasures are really relief from pain, are base pleasures shared with animals, and quickly pass away.
rows.anchor: أنها في الحقيقة ليست لذات بل هي خلاص عن الآلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when pleasurable, they require much toil and bodily pleasures involve foul, repulsive fluids.
rows.anchor: أنها لا تحصل إلا بمتاعب كثيرة ومشاق عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly pleasures do not last and are followed by death, aging, poverty, regret, and fear of death; inviting people to them is deception.
rows.anchor: يتبعها الموت والهرم والفقر والحسرة على الفوت والخوف من الموت

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: One view takes God's servants to mean all morally responsible people; the many verses exempting Satan's followers support that scope.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أبي علي الجبائي

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: On this view Satan and his forces cannot possess people or derange their minds and can only whisper; Satan himself says he had no coercive authority.
rows.anchor: على أنه لا سبيل لإبليس وجنوده على تصريع الناس وتخبيط عقولهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: If Satan could derange minds, he would target virtuous and learned people to maximize harm; mental illness instead arises from corrupt humors, sometimes aggravated by fear of Satan.
rows.anchor: لو قدر على هذه الأعمال لكان يجب أن يتخبط أهل الفضل وأهل العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view restricts God's servants here to people of virtue, knowledge, and faith, since the Quran often uses servants for believers.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن المراد بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God permits Satan to use his full power of whispering, God is more powerful and merciful, repelling Satan's schemes and protecting servants from misguidance.
rows.anchor: فالله تعالى أقدر منه وأرحم بعباده من الكل فهو تعالى يدفع عنه كيد الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that divine protection alone preserves people from sin and error; human beings cannot secure this independently.
rows.anchor: علمنا أن الكل من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi asks whether Satan knew his interlocutor was God, since a direct warning did not deter him, and how he could call the speaker the one who honored Adam if he did not know.
rows.anchor: أن إبليس هل كان عالما بأن الذي تكلم معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that Satan may have been doubtful about everything or may have treated each matter only as a conjecture.
rows.anchor: لعله كان شاكا في الكل أو كان يقول في كل قسم ما يخطر بباله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi asks why God gave Satan respite and enabled temptation despite knowing it would impede His purpose; he says his own school's answer is evident.
rows.anchor: ما الحكمة في أنه تعالى أنظره إلى يوم القيامة ومكنه من الوسوسة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says God knew unbelievers would disbelieve even if Satan did not exist, so Satan's existence adds no harm.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي : علم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: Abu Hashim allows that Satan may add harm but says God left him in place to intensify moral obligation and increase the reward people can earn.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هاشم : لا يبعد أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After digressions, the surah returns to signs of God's power, wisdom, and mercy, especially the benefits He gives people at sea, in service of affirming divine unity.
rows.anchor: عاد إلى ذكر الدلائل الدالة على قدرته وحكمته ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuzjī means to drive or move something along gradually, stage after stage; the same word appears in the description of a paltry payment.
rows.anchor: والإزجاء سوق الشيء حالا بعد حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God moves ships across the sea so people can seek His bounty through trade; the general address refers to everyone, and mercy here means worldly benefits and interests.
rows.anchor: يسير الفلك على وجه البحر لتبتغوا من فضله في طلب التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fear of drowning, people call on God alone rather than idols, the sun and moon, angels, or celestial spheres; once rescued to land they turn from faith and sincerity, displaying ingratitude.
rows.anchor: لا يتضرع إلى الصنم والشمس والقمر والملك والفلك

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Khasf means something entering into something else; examples include a sunken eye or spring and an eclipse, which seems to hide the sun.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : الخسف والخسوف هو دخول الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land is called its side because the preceding verse named the sea; as God can make people disappear beneath water, He can bury them beneath soil.
rows.anchor: ذكر البحر في الآية الأولى فهو جانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rescue from the sea does not make people safe on land: God can punish from below by subsidence or from above by stones, so they should call on Him in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: أما من جانب التحت فبالخسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasb means throwing; a hasib may be a punishment that pelts people with stones, a wind carrying dust and pebbles, or a cloud throwing hail.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الحصب في اللغة : الرمي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines hasib as soil containing pebbles, with hasib describing something possessing those pebbles.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : الحاصب التراب الذي فيه حصباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wakil in this context is a helper who protects people from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني لا تجدوا ناصرا ينصركم ويصونكم من عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat asks whether God may return people to the sea and send a violent wind that breaks the ship and sinks them.
rows.anchor: أي في البحر تارة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasif describes a forcefully breaking wind; the verb qasafa means to break something violently, and here the wind smashes ships and drowns their passengers.
rows.anchor: والقاصف من الريح التي تكسر الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their drowning would be because of their disbelief.
rows.anchor: أي بسبب كفركم ثم لا تجدوا لكم علينا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that no one would follow up to object to God's act and turn its punishment away; tabīʿ means follower.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : أي لا تجدوا من يتبعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the five verbs with first-person plural nūn; the remaining readers use third-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو جميع هذه الخمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading continues the preceding third-person construction; the nūn reading is also sound because clauses may shift between persons while retaining one meaning.
rows.anchor: فلأن ما قبله على الواحد الغائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse gathers four kinds of divine favor that distinguish human beings; the first is their special honor.
rows.anchor: ذكر الله تعالى في هذه الآية أربعة أنواع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being combines soul and body; the human soul is the noblest soul and the human body the noblest body in the lower world.
rows.anchor: فالنفس الإنسانية أشرف النفوس الموجودة في العالم السفلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human soul shares nutrition, growth, reproduction, sensation, and voluntary movement with plant and animal life, but uniquely has a rational faculty that knows realities and receives knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: النفس الإنسانية مختصة بقوة أخرى وهي القوة العاقلة المدركة لحقائق الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rational faculty surpasses bodily and animal powers; Razi points to twenty arguments he gave under the verse about God as the Light of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: ذكرنا هناك عشرين وجها في بيان أن القوة العقلية أجل وأعلى من القوة الجسمية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says, in a report transmitted by Maymun ibn Mihran, that humans alone eat with their hands while other creatures eat with their mouths.
rows.anchor: روى ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: At a meal hosted by al-Rashid, Abu Yusuf cites the saying attributed to his grandfather that God honored humans by giving them fingers to eat with, prompting the caliph to put away spoons.
rows.anchor: وعنده أبو يوسف ، فقال له

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies human honor with speech and discernment; Razi explains that human beings can communicate all they know, unlike other animals.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : قال الضحاك : بالنطق والتمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings can define and convey what they know, while other animals cannot give a full account of inward pain or pleasure; this capacity defines rational speech.
rows.anchor: فهو الإنسان ، فإنه يمكنه تعريف غيره كل ما عرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mute person remains included because gestures and writing convey meaning; a parrot's limited imitation does not amount to complete communication.
rows.anchor: ظهر أن الإنسان الأخرس داخل في هذا الوصف

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata's view is that human beings are honored by their upright, extended stature.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : قال عطاء : بامتداد القامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Height by itself cannot explain human distinction, since trees are taller; intellect and sensory and motor powers must also be considered.
rows.anchor: لأن الأشجار أطور من قامة الإنسان بل ينبغي أن يشترط فيه شرط

rows.speaker: بيان
rows.claim: Bayan says the honor is the beauty of human form and cites God's shaping of people and praise of human creation.
rows.anchor: قال بيان بحسن الصورة ، والدليل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi depicts the eye's carefully arranged dark and light rings as one example of the beauty of the human body.
rows.anchor: فتأمل عضوا واحدا من أعضاء الإنسان وهو العين فخلق الحدقة سوداء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify writing as a distinctive honor granted to humanity.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم من كرامات الآدمي أن آتاه الله الخط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing lets later scholars preserve and expand earlier learning, so sciences, virtues, and religious and intellectual investigations develop cumulatively.
rows.anchor: ويضم كل متأخر مباحث كثيرة إلى علم المتقدمين كثرت العلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran associates this full honor of writing with God's teaching by the pen and teaching humanity what it did not know.
rows.anchor: بالقلم * علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four simple elements serve human beings: earth is a nurturing home, water supports drinking and agriculture, air sustains life and disperses decay, and fire cooks, lights, and warms.
rows.anchor: أما الأرض فهي لنا كالأم الحاضنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea also serves human beings with fresh meat, ornaments, and ships sailing through it.
rows.anchor: سخر البحر لنأكل منه لحما طريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem says that a person seeking winter fruit finds it in the fire of winter, illustrating fire's benefits in darkness and cold.
rows.anchor: ومن يرد في الشتاء فاكهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upper atmospheric phenomena, minerals, plants, and animals together serve humanity, which presides over and benefits from the world as a ruler over a populated settlement.
rows.anchor: هذا العالم بأسره جار مجرى قرية معمورة أو خان معد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creatures fall into four classes: intellect without appetite (angels), appetite without intellect (beasts), neither (plants and inanimate things), and both (humans); humans surpass beasts and inanimate beings, though angels raise a separate question.
rows.anchor: المخلوقات تنقسم إلى أربعة أقسام إلى ما حصلت له القوة العقلية الحكمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of four modes of existence, God alone is eternal and everlasting; the transient world is lowest, an eternal but non-everlasting being is impossible, while humans and angels are everlasting and thus nobler than the transient world.
rows.anchor: وإما أن لا يكون أزليا ولكنه يكون أبديا ، وهو الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upper world is nobler than the lower; the human spirit belongs to the upper, holy order, and is uniquely present among the lower world's creatures.
rows.anchor: وروح الإنسان من جنس الأرواح العلوية والجواهر القدسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearest being to God is the noblest; humans approach through hearts illuminated by knowledge, tongues in remembrance, and limbs in obedience, and all their possible perfections come from God's gift.
rows.anchor: قلبه مستنير بمعرفة الله تعالى ولسانه مشرف بذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's generosity toward humanity spans creation, upbringing, and the final stage of human life, as shown by verses on the pen and God's gracious address to humanity.
rows.anchor: ووصف نفسه بالتكريم عند تربيته للإنسان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say God created Adam with His own hand while creating other beings by the command Be; this expresses greater care for Adam and dignity for his descendants.
rows.anchor: هذا التكريم معناه أنه تعالى خلق آدم بيده وخلق غيره بطريق كن فيكون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says people are carried over land on horses, mules, donkeys, and camels, and over sea in ships.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في البر على الخيل والبغال والحمير والإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The animals, water, and ships are subjected to human use for travel, defense, warfare, and livelihood, making humanity like ruler over its dependents.
rows.anchor: سخر هذه الدواب له حتى يركبها ويحمل عليها ويغزو ويقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans receive the finest animal and plant foods, purified, cooked, and fully prepared for consumption.
rows.anchor: يتغذى الإنسان منه بألطف أنواعها وأشرف أقسامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honor refers to natural endowments such as intellect, speech, writing, beauty, and stature; preference refers to using them to acquire true beliefs and virtuous character.
rows.anchor: الأول هو التكريم والثاني هو التفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says humans are preferred over many creatures, not all; those who draw the implication identify angels as beings above humans.
rows.anchor: فهذا يدل على أنه حصل في مخلوقات الله تعالى شيء لا يكون الإنسان مفضلا عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas holds that angels are better than humans; al-Zajjaj also adopts this view, as al-Wahidi reports.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول مذهب ابن عباس واختيار الزجاج على ما رواه الواحدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether prophets or angels are superior was treated at length under the command that the angels prostrate to Adam.
rows.anchor: وقد سبق ذكر هذه المسألة بالاستقصاء في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: A report from Zayd ibn Aslam says angels asked why humans received worldly pleasures and asks that they receive such gifts in the afterlife; God swears that Adam's descendants, created by His hand, will not be treated like those created by Be.
rows.anchor: روي عن زيد بن أسلم أنه قال : قالت الملائكة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says a believer is more honored by God than the angels who are near Him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه : المؤمن أكرم على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who claim angels are categorically superior rely on an argument from the verse's implied contrast, but Razi calls this a weak proof.
rows.anchor: وهو في الحقيقة تمسك بدليل الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading is reported with yāʾ or nūn, in passive form, and as al-Hasan's active yāʾ reading; al-Farra and grammarians reject the last form's basis, perhaps due to a reporter mistaking a mixed-vowel passive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن يدعو كل أناس قال الفراء وأهل العربية لا يعرفون وجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is accusative through an implied remember; it cannot be governed by the past verb We favored, though that may be understood prospectively as God's future honor and reward.
rows.anchor: يوم ندعو نصب بإضمار اذكر ولا يجوز أن يقال العامل فيه قوله وفضلناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An imam is anyone a group follows, whether rightly or wrongly: a prophet for his community, a caliph for his subjects, the Quran for Muslims, or a prayer leader.
rows.anchor: الإمام في اللغة كل من ائتم به قوم كانوا على هدى أو ضلالة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report attributed in prophetic form to Abu Hurayra says imam means each community's prophet; people are summoned as followers of Abraham, Moses, Jesus, or Muhammad, and the truthful receive books in their right hands.
rows.anchor: إمامهم نبيهم روي ذلك مرفوعا عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the prophet interpretation, the preposition means following or allegiance, like being called by one's name, or it introduces a circumstantial phrase with the community gathered around its imam.
rows.anchor: أن يكون التقدير يدعو كل أناس بإمامهم تبعا وشيعة لأمامهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd interpret imam as the revealed scripture of each community, so people are called as followers of the Quran, Torah, or Gospel.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الضحاك وابن زيد بإمامهم أي بكتابهم الذي أنزل عليهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Rabi, and Abu al-Aliya say imam is the record containing people's deeds, which is called imam in the Quran; here the preposition means with.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن بكتابهم الذي فيه أعمالهم وهو قول الربيع وأبي العالية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the interpretation of imam as a plural meaning mothers an outlandish exegesis, and sarcastically questions whether its linguistic claim or its proposed wisdom is stranger.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير أن الإمام جمع أم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That rejected interpretation says people are summoned by their mothers to honor Jesus and Hasan and Husayn and avoid exposing children born outside marriage.
rows.anchor: الحكمة في الدعاء بالأمهات دون الآباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi proposes that a person's dominant inner trait functions as an imam: moral dispositions drive outward deeds, on which resurrection's reward and punishment depend.
rows.anchor: فذلك الخلق الباطن كالإمام له والملك المطاع والرئيس المتبوع

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the plural demonstrative by taking whoever as collective; fatil is the fine husk in a date stone's groove and exemplifies the tiniest imaginable amount.
rows.anchor: إنما قال أولئك لأن من أوتي في معنى الجمع والفتيل القشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatil is described as a negligible amount: those given their record in the right hand lose none of their reward, even by the smallest measure.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا ينقصون من الثواب بمقدار فتيل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid transmits Ibn Abbas's explanation that fatil is the grime produced by rolling the thumb against the index finger; the word reflects twisting.
rows.anchor: وروى مجاهد عن ابن عباس أنه قال الفتيل هو الوسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The left-handed also see their books, but fear and distress at the grave sins written there make their tongues heavy; the right-handed read clearly and even invite the assembly to read their books.
rows.anchor: وأما أصحاب اليمين فأمرهم على عكس ذلك لا جرم أنهم يقرؤون كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ in the treatment of the first and second a'ma: some apply imala only to the first, some pronounce both open, and others apply imala to both.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم ونصر عن الكسائي ومن كان في هذه أعمى

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi explains that the first a'ma is an ordinary adjective and accepts imala, whereas the second means more blind as a comparative and does not accept it; the readings thus distinguish the senses.
rows.anchor: الوجه في تصحيح قراءة أبي عمرو أن المراد بالأعمى في الكلمة الأولى كونه في نفسه أعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first blindness is certainly blindness of the heart; the second may also be spiritual, with several explanations, or it may refer to physical sight.
rows.anchor: عمى البصر بل المراد منه عمى القلب

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: When a Yemeni visitor asked Ibn Abbas, he pointed to the preceding favors: whoever is blind to blessings witnessed in this life is even blinder about the unseen afterlife; this refers back to those blessings.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة : جاء نفر من أهل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak and Abu Waraq, explains that one blind to God's evident power in creation is more blind to the afterlife; here this world is meant by this.
rows.anchor: روى أبو ورق عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال من كان في الدنيا أعمى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says a misguided unbeliever is more lost in the afterlife because repentance and escape from afflictions remain possible in this life but not there.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن من كان في الدنيا ضالا كافرا فهو في الآخرة أعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual blindness in the afterlife cannot mean ignorance of God, whom its inhabitants know necessarily; it means blindness to the road to Paradise.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن حمل العمى الثاني على الجهل بالله لأن أهل الآخرة يعرفون الله بالضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation links worldly blindness to greed and delight in worldly pleasures; desire and regret intensify in the afterlife, leaving the person in darkness without knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: لشدة حرصهم على تحصيل الدنيا وابتهاجهم بلذاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second broad interpretation takes the later blindness literally: those blind in heart here are raised physically blind, as other verses say.
rows.anchor: أن يحمل العمى الثاني على عمى العين والبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting divine favors and the ranks of the afterlife, God warns the fortunate against being deceived by the manipulative arguments of those in error.
rows.anchor: أردفه بما يجري مجرى تحذير السعداء من الاغترار بوساوس أرباب الضلال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says the Thaqif delegation asked the Prophet to let them honor al-Lat for a year and make their valley sacred like Mecca; when they urged him to attribute the concession to God, Umar rebuked them and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء نزلت هذه الآية في وفد ثقيف

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports that Thaqif dictated a pact exempting them from taxes, mobilization, and tribute; when the Prophet fell silent, Umar drew his sword and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: صاحب ( الكشاف ) أنهم جاءوا بكاتبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Thaqif accounts occurred in Medina and thus support classifying these verses as Medinan.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذه القصة إنما وقعت بالمدينة فلهذا السبب قالوا إن هذه الآيات مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Quraysh asked Muhammad to exchange verses of mercy and punishment so that they would believe.
rows.anchor: قريشا قالوا له : اجعل آية رحمة آية عذاب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Quraysh detained the Prophet at Mecca before the emigration and asked him to stop insulting their gods; he felt he might stop, making the verse Meccan on this account.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : الكفار أخذوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Quraysh blocked the Prophet from touching the Black Stone unless he touched their idols; he felt an inclination despite disliking the demand, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير أنه عليه السلام كان يستلم الحجر فتمنعه قريش

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the clause means they nearly tempted the Prophet; inna is a lightened emphatic particle, the lām distinguishes it from negation, and fitna originally means testing gold by melting it to separate good from bad.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج معنى الكلام كادوا يفتنونك ودخلت إن واللام للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna broadened from testing to removing something from its proper course; the opponents sought to divert Muhammad from the Quran's guidance by making him invent a divine command.
rows.anchor: أي يزيلونك ويصرفونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had he complied, they would have made him their close friend and publicly treated him as approving their polytheism.
rows.anchor: لو فعلت ما أرادوا لاتخذوك خليلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the slight inclination as the Prophet's silence when they pressed their request.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد حيث سكت عن جوابهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that after this verse was revealed the Prophet prayed, asking God not to leave him to himself even for an instant.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة لما نزلت هذه الآية قال النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled punishment means twice the punishment of worldly life and twice that of the afterlife; doubling adds a like amount to the original, and punishment is understood from context.
rows.anchor: ضعف عذاب الحياة وضعف عذاب الممات يريد عذاب الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran elsewhere calls punishment doubled, supporting the implied punishment in this verse.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم في القرآن من وصف العذاب بالضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened doubling reflects prophets' greater blessings, which make their sins graver and the punishment due for them greater; the Quran gives a parallel warning to the Prophet's wives.
rows.anchor: أن أقسام نعم الله تعالى في حق الأنبياء عليهم السلام أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith about the initiator of an evil practice bearing followers' sins might imply punishment beyond double; Razi replies that proving a double does not exclude additional punishment, and limiting it would rely on weak implied contrast.
rows.anchor: إثبات الضعف لا يدل على نفي الزائد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After such punishment, the Prophet would find no one able to rescue him from God's judgment.
rows.anchor: لم تجد أحدا يخلصك من عذابنا وعقابنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics of prophetic impeccability claim the verse implies a near forgery against God, a near inclination toward the unbelievers' religion absent divine support, and a prior offense that would explain the threat.
rows.anchor: احتج الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāda means nearness rather than occurrence, so the verse does not say that Muhammad actually fell into the temptation.
rows.anchor: كاد معناه المقاربة فكان معنى الآية أنه قرب وقوعه في الفتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional laula says that God's actual strengthening prevented the inclination from occurring.
rows.anchor: معناه أنه حصل تثبيت الله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A severe warning does not prove a sin was committed; the Quran issues comparable conditional threats elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك التهديد على المعصية لا يدل على الإقدام عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's school argues that only God's enabling preserves people from sin, since even the Prophet would have inclined without God's strengthening.
rows.anchor: بأنه لا عصمة عن المعاصي إلا بتوفيق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites interpret strengthening as God's subtle deterrent aids, such as recalling promise, threat, and the fact that he was God's prophet.
rows.anchor: المراد بهذا التثبيت الألطاف الصارفة له عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that the need for a divinely supplied deterrent shows an impulse to the forbidden action existed; God's act prevented it, consistent with the view that power together with motive necessitates action unless opposed by another motive.
rows.anchor: لو لم يوجد المقتضى للإقدام على ذلك العمل المحذور

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the passage can be read without tying it to a particular occasion because the polytheists repeatedly tried to divert the Prophet from his religion.
rows.anchor: يمكن أيضا تأويلها من غير تقييد بسبب يضاف نزولها فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They proposed reciprocal worship of one another's gods, prompting the command to declare that the Prophet worships none of what they worship.
rows.anchor: الكافرون * لا أعبد ما تعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wanted the Prophet to compromise so they could compromise in return.
rows.anchor: ودوا لو تدهن فيدهنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They offered abundant wealth and beautiful women if he would abandon his prophetic claim; the Quran answered by telling him not to covet worldly splendor.
rows.anchor: وعرضوا عليه الأموال الكثيرة والنسوان الجميلة ليترك ادعاء النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demanded that the Prophet expel believers, and revelation forbade him from driving away those who call on God.
rows.anchor: ودعوه إلى طرد المؤمنين عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These varied efforts illustrate the opponents' attempt to remove the Prophet from his course, while God keeps him firm on the straight religion and path.
rows.anchor: فبين تعالى أنه يثبته على الدين القويم والمنهج المستقيم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Meccans intended to expel the Prophet; God prevented them until He ordered the emigration, and they would have been destroyed quickly if they had forced him out.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : هم أهل مكة هموا بإخراج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the Quraysh did not survive long after the Prophet left Mecca before God killed them at Badr.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives a Medinan account: jealous Jews urged Muhammad to go to Syria, promising belief and followership if he overcame fear of the Romans; he camped at Dhu al-Hulayfa before the verse sent him back.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the Meccan account because the surah is Meccan; the land means Mecca on that account and Medina on Ibn Abbas's alternative.
rows.anchor: فالقول الأول اختيار الزجاج وهو الوجه لأن السورة مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ard can name a particular place rather than the whole earth, as in the command to exile people from their places and Joseph's reference to the land he sought for provisions.
rows.anchor: وكثر في التنزيل ذكر الأرض والمراد منها مكان مخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Mecca drove the Prophet out does not contradict this verse: the Meccans only intended to expel him, while he emigrated at God's command.
rows.anchor: إنهم هموا بإخراجه وهو عليه السلام ما خرج بسبب إخراجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read khalafaka with fatḥa, while the other readers have khilafaka; al-Akhfash says the forms mean the same, as in another Quranic use and a poetic line.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو عن عاصم خلفك بفتح الخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's phrase diyār khilāfahum uses khilāf to mean behind or after them.
rows.anchor: عفت الديار خلافهم فكأنما

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Abu's reading makes the verb after idhan subjunctive through idhan's governing effect; the standard reading instead coordinates a verb raised as the predicate of kāda.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي لا يلبثوا على إعمال إذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established custom is to destroy peoples who expel their prophet; sunnah is an emphatic verbal noun here.
rows.anchor: أن كل قوم أخرجوا نبيهم من ظهرانيهم فسنة الله أن يهلكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can alter God's customary ordering: an event's particular time and qualities come from divine specification, not its own essence, or it would persist forever and not differ from its like.
rows.anchor: اختصاص كل حادث بوقته المعين وصفته المعينة ليس أمرا ثابتا له لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the specifying will, power, or knowledge were created, it would require another specification without end; if eternal, it cannot change, so the specified events cannot change either.
rows.anchor: إن كانت حادثة افتقر حدوثها إلى تخصيص آخر ولزم التسلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from God's doctrines about divinity, resurrection, and prophethood to the command of worship; after faith, prayer is the most excellent act of obedience.
rows.anchor: أردفها بذكر الأمر بالطاعات بعد الإيمان وأشرف الطاعات بعد الإيمان الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the threat that opponents might expel him, prayer directs the Prophet to persist in worship, trusting God to defeat their plots and raise his religion above theirs.
rows.anchor: أمره تعالى بالإقبال على عبادته لكي ينصره عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the report that Jews urged a move to Syria, the response is that God is Lord in every land and victory comes through His aid; the Prophet should continue prayer, return to his home, and ask for truthful entry and exit and a supporting authority there.
rows.anchor: المعبود واحد في كل البلاد وما النصرة والدولة إلا بتأييده ونصرته

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A view transmitted from Ali defines the sun's duluk as sunset.
rows.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام أنه قال : دلوك الشمس غروبها

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud likewise says, in a report through Zirr ibn Hubaysh, that duluk is sunset.
rows.anchor: أن عبد الله بن مسعود قال : دلوك الشمس غروبها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn Abbas the view that duluk is sunset.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير هذا القول عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra and Ibn Qutayba adopt the sunset interpretation of duluk.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول اختيار الفراء وابن قتيبة من المتأخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority of Companions and Successors hold that duluk is the sun's decline from its zenith.
rows.anchor: أن دلوك الشمس هو زوالها عن كبد السماء وهو اختيار الأكثرين

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: A report from Jabir says that after the Prophet and Companions ate at his home, they left at noon and the Prophet identified that as the time the sun had declined.
rows.anchor: عن جابر أنه قال : ( طعم عندي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf cites a report that Gabriel came at the sun's noon decline and prayed the noon prayer with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: روى صاحب ( الكشاف ) عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says Arabic usage calls the sun dālikah both at noon and at setting because it is declining in either case.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة معنى الدلوك في كلام العرب الزوال

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the root idea of duluk is inclination, which can describe the sun's movement toward either noon decline or sunset.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال : أصل الدلوك الميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers noon decline: since duluk means inclination and the command attaches at its onset, prayer begins when the sun first inclines from the zenith; he calls this a strong argument.
rows.anchor: وجب أن يقال إنه أول ما حصل الميل والزوال تعلق به هذا الحكم

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari also prefers noon decline because prayer from then until night includes four prayers, with dawn recitation adding the fifth; sunset would include only three, and the more useful reading is preferable.
rows.anchor: فإذا حملنا الدلوك على الزوال دخلت الصلوات الخمس في هذه الآية
